# CANON - Addition Scope (Priority Level 2/4)
<!-- AUTO GENERATED from canon.json data via a script - READ ONLY -->

## Permits & Septic

- POLICY: TDEC septic trigger: TDEC septic permitting applies only when the job modifies or installs a septic system — added bedrooms or bathrooms alone do not trigger it; never break ground while TDEC is pending.

## Structure & Site

- DEFAULT: Framing method: Stick-frame for small additions
    Condition: If Unless scope explicitly specifies trusses, roof span exceeds ~24 ft, footprint exceeds ~800 sqft, or the PM confirms trusses
- DEFAULT: Below-grade package: A below-grade package runs between foundation and framing: waterproofing and drainage board on the below-grade wall, foundation drain with filter fabric sloped to daylight, gravel backfill
    Condition: If Sloped-lot or walkout addition — unless engineering specifies otherwise

## Mechanical, Electrical & Plumbing

- POLICY: Electrical service capacity: Existing main-service capacity is verified before any subpanel or HVAC equipment order is placed; a subpanel rides the building permit, a main-service upgrade is its own permit.
- POLICY: Exposed masonry walls in conditioned additions carry an explicit receptacle strategy before electrical rough: When a house-side masonry wall is left exposed inside a conditioned addition, the plan carries a settled receptacle strategy for that wall before the electrical rough task is sized — default is surface raceway (Wiremold-type) on the masonry with NEC 210.52 spacing applied along the full exposed wall length (a ~43 ft wall implies roughly 10 receptacles); the alternative is receptacles confined to the framed walls with the NEC wall-space count reconciled. In-wall boxes are never assumed on an exposed brick or block wall.

## Proposed (machine-derived, UNVETTED — canon above wins on any conflict)

- POLICY: Retained-roof rebuilds keep shoring from before structural demo until the roof is reseated and flashed: When an addition or replacement keeps an existing roof over rebuilt walls, temporary shoring is erected and inspected before any structural demolition, stays through footings, posts, floor and wall framing, and is removed only after the roof bears on the new walls and is flashed; shoring erection is the first demo-phase task and shoring removal is the last framing-phase task. (Unvetted, Confidence 60%)
- POLICY: Roof-cavity insulation under a retained roof settles venting before old vent penetrations are patched closed: When an addition or replacement keeps an existing roof and the rebuilt ceiling is insulated in the rafter bays, the vented-vs-unvented decision (baffles with soffit/ridge or roof vents, or unvented foam at the deck) is settled before any task that patches or closes existing roof vent penetrations, and the roofing patch task carries the resulting vent work rather than closing the cavity blind. (Unvetted, Confidence 50% → Structure & Site)
- DEFAULT: Additions with electrical and mechanical rough carry a six-visit inspection set: Footing, framing, electrical rough, mechanical rough, insulation, and final inspections — six visits at ~2 h each per the card (~12 h), not the 4 h no-MEP bundle. (Unvetted, Confidence 50% → Permits & Septic)
    Condition: If If the addition includes electrical and HVAC rough-in and no plumbing, and the AHJ has not published a different sequence
